findings.title: tnet debug watch-ipn has no --initial-status, and the merged doc misstates Go's flags
findings.detail: Upstream: `tailscale debug watch-ipn` (the subcommand is `watch-ipn`, not `watch-ipn-bus`) starts from mask NotifyNoNetMap and has one flag per bit. `--initial` adds only NotifyInitialState|NotifyInitialPrefs, and a separate `--initial-status` flag (default false) adds NotifyInitialStatus. Merged: the doc comment on run_debug_watch_ipn (src/bin/tnet.rs) says initial_status is left off 'as Go's watch-ipn-bus --initial leaves NotifyInitialStatus off'. That is true of --initial but leaves out that Go offers --initial-status. `tnet debug watch-ipn` is a flagless subcommand that hard-codes initial_state, initial_netmap, prefs, policy and suggested_exit_node to true and initial_status to false, so no CLI path can ask for the snapshot the daemon now serves. Port Go's --initial-status flag (and correct the cited command name).

findings.title: whois user went from always-absent to login-or-display-name, shown for tagged nodes too
findings.detail: Upstream: printWhoIs prints a `User:` block with `who.UserProfile.LoginName` (no fallback to DisplayName) and prints it only when the node is NOT tagged; a tagged node gets `Tags:` instead. Merged: src/ipn/diag.rs changed `user: w.user` to `user: w.user()`. At the old engine pin `WhoIs.user` was documented as always None; at the new pin `WhoIs::user()` returns the profile's login name, else its display name (UserProfile::best_label). So `tnet whois` now prints a `user:` line it never printed before, falls back to a display name where Go prints the (empty) login, and prints it alongside `tags:` for a tagged node whenever control supplies a profile for that node's user id. The change is not mentioned as a behaviour change, has no test, and the docs on WhoisReport (src/localapi.rs) and on diag::whois still say user is 'always None in this fork'. Decide the rule (Go's: LoginName only, untagged only), test it, and fix the docs.

findings.title: A suggestion front-load skipped at subscribe time is never made up, so the watcher can stay without the current pick
findings.detail: Upstream: WatchNotificationsAs calls suggestExitNodeLocked for NotifyInitialSuggestedExitNode whatever the backend state, with no time bound, and puts the id in the first Notify whenever err == nil. The netmap and lastSuggestedExitNode survive `down` (the netmap is only cleared in resetForProfileChangeLocked), so a watcher that subscribes while the node is Stopped or Starting is still front-loaded the pick. Merged: stream_notify settles the front-load as absent when the watch subscribes with no device (daemon down), and bounded_front_load returns None when the device is not Running or the engine takes longer than STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT (500 ms). The front-load is then never retried ('A replacement device is not front-loaded again'). The remembered id is kept across `down` (only logout and profile changes clear it), so when the next `up` recomputes the same pick, publish_suggested_exit_node sees no change and sends nothing. A watcher that asked for the front-load in any of those three cases never learns the node's current suggestion until the pick moves. Either retry the owed front-load on the first epoch that can compute, or send the remembered id.

findings.title: A pick withheld by AllowedSuggestedExitNodes is now pushed to every watcher as an empty id
findings.detail: Upstream: suggestExitNodeUsingDERP and suggestExitNodeUsingTrafficSteering drop peers outside the allow-list BEFORE ranking, so suggestExitNodeLocked sends the best permitted node; the empty StableNodeID goes out only when no permitted candidate exists. Merged: suggested_exit_node_id maps a withheld pick (withheld_by_policy: true) to "", and it is both front-loaded and published to every masked watch. Before this change a withheld pick was silence. Now a tailnet whose best node is outside the allow-list but which has a permitted exit node tells every watcher 'no suggestion', where Go names the permitted node, and it does so on every netmap-driven recompute path, not only on request. The code documents this and the root cause is engine-side (the engine returns one already-chosen node and takes no allow-list; ENGINE_ASKS #44), so the real fix is in the engine, not the daemon.

findings.title: The suggestion compare-and-publish is no longer serialized once the recompute task writes without the backend lock
findings.detail: Upstream: suggestExitNodeLocked runs with b.mu held from the computation through `if prevSuggestion != res.ID { sendToLocked(...) }` and `b.lastSuggestedExitNode = res.ID`, so each change produces exactly one Notify and the stored id is always the latest computation's. Merged: the new per-device task (suggested_exit_node_loop) publishes through a cloned watch::Sender with no lock, while `exit-node suggest` and the watch front-load publish under the backend lock. publish_suggested_exit_node reads the cell (`*cell.borrow() == id`) and then calls send_replace as two separate steps. On the multi-thread runtime two publishers can both pass the compare and both send the same id (a watcher can get the same suggestion frame twice), or an older computation can overwrite a newer one and leave the stale id as the baseline until the next trigger. The Backend field doc still says 'One compare, no second copy to fall out of step'. Make the compare and the store one atomic step (send_if_modified) and serialize the writers.
